text: The prosecution alleged that the in-laws harassed the bride for an additional dowry of ten lakhs, attracting Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
Charges were framed under Section 304B IPC after the deceased wife died of burns within three years of marriage amid persistent dowry demands.
The police filed a chargesheet against the husband and his brother for dowry death following the unnatural death of the woman at her matrimonial home.
The complainant stated that her husband's family confiscated her stridhan and refused to return the jewellery, constituting criminal breach of trust.
An FIR was registered against the father-in-law for abetment of suicide under Section 306 IPC after the daughter-in-law's death.
The trial court convicted the accused husband under Section 498A for subjecting his wife to mental and physical cruelty over four years.
The wife's complaint alleged that the in-laws threatened to throw her out of the matrimonial home unless a car was provided as additional dowry.
The prosecution led evidence that the accused assaulted his spouse with a blunt weapon during a domestic altercation, causing fractures.
A criminal complaint was filed against the husband for wrongful confinement of his wife within the matrimonial house under Section 342 IPC.
An FIR was lodged against the son for criminal breach of trust after he misappropriated funds from his mother's pension account.
The nephew was charged with forgery of a valuable security for creating a false succession certificate in his own name.
The prosecution alleged that the husband forged his wife's signature on the loan documents, an offence under Section 465 IPC.
A complaint of bigamy was filed after evidence emerged that the accused concealed his existing marriage from the second wife.
The accused faced charges under Section 496 IPC for going through a fraudulent marriage ceremony without lawful marriage.
An FIR was registered under Section 363 IPC after the minor girl was taken away from her guardian's custody by a relative.
The accused uncle was charged with abduction of the minor nephew with intent to demand ransom from the family.
A criminal case was initiated against the son-in-law for extortion after he threatened the family to extract money.
An FIR was lodged against the family members for wrongful restraint of the complainant at the matrimonial home.
The accused was booked under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act following a complaint by the child's mother.
The court framed charges of culpable homicide against the accused following the death of his father during a domestic dispute.
A case of criminal conspiracy was registered against the husband and his relatives for planning to dispose of the deceased's body.
The prosecution alleged that the accused issued threats to his wife's parents demanding money, constituting criminal intimidation.
The accused was charged with perjury for giving false evidence about his marital status during the custody proceedings.
An FIR under Section 406 IPC was registered against the husband for dishonestly misappropriating the wife's fixed deposits.
A criminal complaint alleged that the accused destroyed his wife's identity documents to prevent her from leaving the house.
